A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VOLD research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original VOLD benchmark evaluations, component ablations, learning curves and appendix experiments on teacher size, alignment duration and KL masking.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds multimodal capability evaluation, image-based RL experiments and GSPO learning curves in its supplement.

M1.justification: The original SFT alignment, unified RL/distillation objective and reward-guided masking remain unchanged. Sections 7.5–7.6 add procedural variants: further image-text RL from a VOLD checkpoint and substitution of GSPO for GRPO.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original eight benchmark evaluations and Geo3K validation, while adding MME and HallusionBench in Section 7.4. These broaden evaluation substantially toward perception preservation and hallucination, beyond the earlier emphasis on reasoning performance.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Qwen2.5-VL, replicated XReasoner, VLM-R1 and VLAA-Thinker comparisons. New Figure 6 adds standalone GSPO as a comparator to GSPO-VOLD, alongside the existing GRPO comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds supplementary conditions comparing image-based RL initialization and GRPO versus GSPO with and without distillation. It also introduces MME scoring and perception/reasoning breakdowns for MME and MMStar. The original model sizes, training budgets, hyperparameter table and evaluation pipeline remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections 7.4–7.6 investigate whether reasoning training harms perception, whether VOLD provides useful initialization for image-based RL, and whether distillation benefits another RL algorithm. These substantially expand the questions tested; the original alignment, component, teacher-size and masking analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The added results retain point-score and training-curve reporting.

E6.justification: Original numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. v3 adds capability scores, including VOLD's MME score of 2268 and HallusionBench score of 49.8, perception/reasoning breakdowns, image-RL results of 63.4 on MathVista and 38.7 on MathVerse, and GSPO curves. These are substantial new results under added evaluations or training conditions, not revised scores for the original VOLD setting.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the policy definitions and alignment rationale are retained. The GSPO extension is described verbally without adding a formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain text-only reasoning transfer to VLMs, the importance of teacher-aligned SFT and benefits from combining RL with on-policy distillation. Compatibility with other RL algorithms was already claimed in v1; v3 adds supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Section 7.4 newly identifies a perception–reasoning trade-off, attributes it to reasoning-focused training rather than text-only training, and interprets HallusionBench results as evidence against increased hallucination. Sections 7.5–7.6 further discuss VOLD as initialization for image-based RL and its applicability beyond GRPO. These materially extend the earlier interpretations and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: The core implementation details, GPU counts, preprocessing, hyperparameters and project-page disclosure are retained. However, v1's direct Mixture-of-Thoughts source URL is omitted from the corresponding v3 bibliography entry, reducing explicit data-access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion distinguishing VOLD from Thinking Machines Lab's text-only on-policy distillation, plus references supporting GSPO, the new benchmarks and the perception–reasoning trade-off. The central positioning relative to KDRL and X-Reasoner remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained, with localized abstract, introduction, caption and conclusion edits. v3 separates policy and component ablations into Sections 4.3–4.4, moves learning dynamics into Section 4.5, and renumbers the appendices as supplementary Sections 6–7.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column layout to two columns, with extensive resizing and repositioning of existing figures and tables and revised caption placement. v3 also adds Tables 6–7 and Figure 6; the original visual evidence remains present.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 and Figure 6 improve empirical support by exposing perception losses, testing image-based RL initialization and substantiating the previously asserted compatibility with other RL algorithms. The gains are limited by sparse training details for the new experiments and an attribution of perception loss to reasoning training that the comparisons do not causally isolate. The core method and original results remain unchanged.
